Welcome—I'm glad you're here.
Grief—it can sweep in like a storm, or linger quietly like a shadow. It reshapes the world you thought you knew, turning everyday moments upside down in ways that just don't seem to make sense.
Together, we're going to explore this experience through the words of Joan Didion in her remarkable book, The Year of Magical Thinking. She invites us into a journey where loss is sudden and the boundaries between memory, reality, and hope start to blur.
Have you ever found yourself bargaining with fate, searching desperately for meaning when nothing seems to add up? Maybe you've clung to old rituals, hoping they'd anchor you. It's all a part of survival—a way the heart tries to hold on to what’s gone, while learning to move forward with what remains.
What we'll discover together is that mourning isn't something you can plot on a straight line. It's unpredictable—there are moments of piercing clarity, then times when everything feels confusing and fragile. And yet, within all that, there's resilience, vulnerability, and a quiet strength as we try to make sense of the changes loss brings.
As we follow Didion’s deeply personal journey, we'll notice how the simplest routines—meals, conversations, even just getting through the day—become transformed. Absence is everywhere, and so is the longing for what once was. Her story weaves together memories, hard facts, and reflections on what it means to heal, showing us that sometimes, logic just isn't enough to hold back the tide of emotion.
So, as we step into this year of magical thinking, let’s open ourselves to the possibility of finding meaning in the messiness of grief—of seeing love, resilience, and hope not as answers, but as companions on the journey.
I hope you’ll join me in exploring these questions and feelings, and that together, we’ll discover not just the pain of loss, but the enduring power of what remains.
